title: Luanda civic march on living costs, jobs and local elections
location: Luanda; organizers set off from the Santa Ana Cemetery parking area toward Largo do 1.º de Maio/Largo da Independência; reporting differs on the route and stopping point
organizer: Civil-society/youth organizers including Pedrowsky Teca and Adolfo Campos
participants_original: Centenas de jovens (hundreds of young people); no exact count reported
threshold_50_evidence: DW reports hundreds of young people gathered in Luanda; this qualitative estimate clearly exceeds 50, but the exact total is not reported.

start_date.summary: Both contemporaneous reports identify the march as occurring Thursday, Dec. 10.

end_date.summary: The Dec. 10 report says the demonstration ended before the planned 22:00 finish; no exact ending time is reported.

location.summary: DW places participants at Largo da Independência; Angola24Horas describes a march from Santa Ana cemetery toward Largo do 1.º de Maio; Correio da Kianda reports the planned route toward Largo Primeiro de Maio. Exact route/stopping point varies by account.

organizer.summary: DW names activist Pedrowsky Teka as an organizer; Angola24Horas quotes organizer Adolfo Campos; the pre-event notice identifies a civil-society coordination.

demands.summary: Reports describe demands regarding high cost of living, local elections, employment, corruption, and broader civic/political change. Coded political process and prices/costs; jobs are noted in prose.

participants_original.summary: DW reports hundreds of young Angolans; no exact count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound is published; left null.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound is published; left null.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The contemporary report’s qualitative estimate of hundreds supports the 50-person threshold without an exact count.

protester_violence.summary: DW describes the demonstration as without violence and Angola24Horas describes it as a peaceful march; no violence by participants is reported.

state_response.summary: Police accompanied/secured the march. Angola24Horas quotes an organizer saying some detentions had occurred, without a number; Correio da Kianda relays police statements about a route deviation and statue action. Other response categories remain unknown.

notes: Public Luanda gathering with an explicit state/policy target and a clear qualitative estimate above 50. Employment is a reported demand but does not map to a dedicated category in the supplied extension list. The event is reported peaceful, while one organizer says unspecified detentions occurred; those are separate fields. Do not transfer violence or deaths from earlier October/November events to this march.
open_questions: No exact count or count range is reported.
The organizer-reported detentions are not enumerated or independently confirmed in the available opened sources.
Accounts differ on route/stopping point and say the event ended before its planned close; precise endpoint/time remain unknown.

title: Luanda march protesting the Constitutional Court’s refusal to legalize PRA-JA
location: Luanda; from the Santa Ana Cemetery to Maianga, near the city centre; reported route about eight kilometres
organizer: PRA-JA Servir Angola installation committee; Abel Chivukuvuku led the march, with reported participants from civic and other political groups
participants_original: Perto de 600 manifestantes (nearly 600 demonstrators); no exact count
threshold_50_evidence: The Lusa-attributed account reports nearly 600 participants, clearly above 50; numeric range is not inferred from ‘nearly’. The account is also reproduced in other outlets, which are not treated as independent confirmation.

start_date.summary: Novo Jornal’s Lusa-attributed report identifies Saturday, Dec. 19 as the march date; Esquerda’s search-result page caption also identifies Luanda on Dec. 19.

end_date.summary: The report says the march covered about eight kilometres and ended in Maianga on Saturday; no time is given.

location.summary: The report places assembly by Santa Ana cemetery and the end in Maianga after an approximately eight-kilometre march.

organizer.summary: The march was called by Abel Chivukuvuku and the PRA-JA installation committee; other political/civic actors are mentioned, including Bloco Democrático.

demands.summary: The main reported demand was reversal/review of the Constitutional Court decision refusing to legalize PRA-JA. Participants also voiced broad dissatisfaction with hardship and the governing MPLA; the specific coded demand is political behaviour/process.

participants_original.summary: The Lusa-attributed Novo Jornal report says nearly 600 people; the exact count is not known.

participants_min.summary: No numeric interval can be calculated from ‘nearly 600’; left null.

participants_max.summary: No numeric interval can be calculated from ‘nearly 600’; left null.

protester_violence.summary: The Lusa-attributed account calls the march peaceful/orderly and quotes no vandalism or physical harm; Esquerda’s search result says it concluded without incident.

state_response.summary: The article says police prevented marchers from reaching the Constitutional Court while securing the route. It gives no report of arrests, beatings, shootings, deaths, dispersal, ignoring, or accommodation; those dimensions remain unknown.

notes: A documented public demonstration and state-targeted legal-process demand, with a Lusa-origin estimate near 600. Club-K and Ver Angola copies returned HTTP 403; Novo Jornal’s separately accessible Lusa-attributed article was opened and is the evidentiary basis. Do not count multiple Lusa publications as independent. Review the manual’s political-rally exclusion: PRA-JA is a party seeking participation in 2022, but this march opposed a Constitutional Court registration decision and participants also expressed broader anti-government grievances; the result remains pending review.
open_questions: Potential political-rally exclusion because the organizer is a party preparing for 2022 elections; assess whether this was a state-directed protest over judicial registration rather than election support.
The report’s near-600 estimate is approximate; exact count and range are unknown.

The Lusa copies give inconsistent apparent dates (one page is dated Dec. 20, but Novo Jornal’s body identifies Saturday Dec. 19); use Dec. 19 based on the explicit event-day account, retain discrepancy for review.
The article describes police blocking access to the court but also securing the march; codeable response category remains unresolved/unknown.

title: Supreme Court employees strike over pay disparity
location: Supreme Court, Luanda; exact location of any public gathering not reported
organizer: Supreme Court employees; union committee coordinator Domingos Fernandes Feca is quoted
participants_original: Supreme Court employees/workers; no count reported

start_date.summary: DW says the stoppage began Thursday, Dec. 17.

end_date.summary: No end date or later report of continued activity located; unknown.

location.summary: The employees are those of the Supreme Court, but the report does not give the physical strike/gathering location.

organizer.summary: A court employee union committee coordinator is quoted; no separate organizer group name is provided.

demands.summary: Reports describe a wage disparity against workers of other superior courts and a demand for salary improvements.

participants_original.summary: Only the plural ‘workers/employees’ is reported; no number.

participants_min.summary: No numeric lower bound published; null.

participants_max.summary: No numeric upper bound published; null.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence that 50 people participated or gathered in public; threshold remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: No accessed source states this field; it remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No accessed source states this field; it remains unknown.

notes: The employer is a state court and the demand concerns public-sector salary parity, but reporting documents a work stoppage, not a street/public gathering, and gives no participant count. Keep as a candidate pending proof of a public gathering and at least 50 participants; do not infer threshold from the word ‘workers’. The strike was current on Dec. 18; its end is unknown.
open_questions: Was there a public gathering or only a workplace stoppage?
When did the strike end and what state response occurred?

title: Former Sonangol contractor workers hold vigil over dismissal and employment claims
location: In front of Sonangol headquarters, Luanda
organizer: Former employees of Sonangol service-provider companies; worker spokesperson Carlos Alberto is quoted
participants_original: Um grupo de trabalhadores despedidos (a group of dismissed workers); no count reported

start_date.summary: On Dec. 18 the report calls this the fifth day of a vigil and sixth day of a strike; the exact day of onset is not stated. Month precision is secure, day precision is not.

location.summary: DW explicitly places a group of former contractor workers in front of Sonangol headquarters.

organizer.summary: The group consists of dismissed workers from companies serving Sonangol; spokesperson Carlos Alberto is quoted.

demands.summary: The workers protest alleged illegal dismissal, demand employment status under Presidential Decree 31/17 and seek wages calculated at the exchange rate; classified as labor/wage dispute.

participants_original.summary: The source says a group of dismissed workers; it publishes no size.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No published count or other evidence that the group reached 50; threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: No accessed source states this field; it remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No accessed source states this field; it remains unknown.

notes: A group of dismissed workers is reported holding a public vigil outside a state oil company headquarters and invoking a presidential decree, which makes the target plausibly state-linked; the stated grievances also concern the employer and contractor companies. The source reports this on Dec. 18 as the fifth day of a vigil/sixth day of strike, so onset is recorded only at month precision. No count confirms the 50-person threshold.
open_questions: How many workers were at the vigil?
Does the action meet the threshold and public-assembly definition?
Exact vigil/strike onset and end dates remain uncertain.
Whether the demand was directed to state policy/Sonangol rather than only private contractors needs reviewer attention.
